Beginning a read-only adversarial review of the P9.1 change.

The review targets six areas: exec/v1 schema compatibility, malformed input handling, semantic errors, fixtures, documentation, and neutral registrar ownership. Only one pass is permitted with no recursive fixes or tool calls. Findings must be reported as JSON only. Only reproducible correctness or contract issues gate a RED status; speculative nits are discarded.

Checking the specification for commit ownership. The executor commits product files after finish or unit acceptance. The reviewer writes review reports without committing product files. The fixer commits fixes according to review reports. In native Task mode the session itself calls these operations. In orchestration the coordinator handles commits while executor and reviewer workers do not.

Commit-to-plan linkage is enforced by the engine via git trailers. The commit containing a `finish` record cannot write its own plan link, so `Plan`, `Plan-Ref`, and `Plan-Role` trailers carry the reference. Plans resolve commits through `plan.py commits`. The helper prints the SHA for the engine to stage. Pre-made commits remain supported via `finish --commit SHA`. Outside these rules are push, merge, tag, release, `--amend`, and `--no-verify`. The schema defines `commitRole` as an enum of `executor`, `reviewer`, and `fix`.

The `commit` object in the run-policy requires `scope`, `roles`, and `message_convention`. Scope is an enum of `item` or `unit`. Roles is a non-empty array of commit roles. The message convention references a task-specific identifier that orchestration does not know.

Semantic checks flag a `COMMIT_POLICY_CONFLICT` when `commit` is present but `git_action` is `none`. A `git_action: commit` without `commit` is allowed for legacy documents. Roles must not contain duplicates.

The `stage-result.commits` array requires four fields per entry: `sha`, `role`, `ref`, and `paths_digest`. All are mandatory and no extra properties are permitted. Each SHA must be unique within the array.

The `paths_digest` value is the SHA-256 hex of a sorted list of repository-relative POSIX paths joined by newlines, with no trailing newline.

Fixtures cover valid and invalid commit cases. Valid examples include `run-policy/commit-policy.json` and `stage-result/with-commits.json`. Invalid examples include `run-policy/commit-with-git-none.json`, `stage-result/commit-bad-role.json`, and `stage-result/commit-duplicate-sha.json`.

Documentation in `docs/contracts.md` lists table rows for `run-policy` and `stage-result`.
